axes.text: A frozen material-association tracker (Jaccard>=0.30) achieves zero erroneous cross-population transfers across 72 traces. The original Stage 6.11 tracker's '3/5 successful' claim was withdrawn.
Pooled random/fixed forcing does not generically move the flock (CI spans zero), but this hides real per-state heterogeneity -- some seeds show demonstrable effects, others are clean negatives.

No static actuator feature (kinematic score, historical authority, dev-selected best set) beats random on held-out evaluation. The apparent 6.9x oracle advantage is winner's-curse: stable actuator identity explains under 1% of outcome variance on average and collapses under a permutation null.

Closure A (8 states, 240 rollouts): every class-level 90% CI (core, boundary, live parent, non-parent) spans zero; pooled interior-vs-exterior effect spans zero with inconsistent sign (5/8 states positive, 3/8 negative). No stable organizational-role privilege demonstrated.

Closure B (same rollouts): the true directed FOV-gated live_edges relation and short temporal reachability are statistically indistinguishable from plain geometric contact (all per-state correlation CIs span zero and overlap heavily). Live exterior parents did not outperform near exterior non-parents despite being ~9x closer to the target on average.

Closure C (n=3 usable states, disclosed sparsity): pooled within-onset actuator spread (0.0109) exceeds pooled onset-time range (0.0040); only 1/3 states shows onset dominating. Timing variation is NOT shown to dominate actuator-identity variation in this bounded sample.
Short K=1 schedules preserve identity validity at high rates; longer/larger (K>=2, d=24) schedules show materially elevated target-loss. K=1 at d=24 showed no elevated loss -- cardinality-specific.

final_decision: Decision-language branch: 'none of these are strong'. No stable spatial/organizational actuator interface was demonstrated (Closure A); true directed causal-interface membership showed no discernible advantage over geometric proximity, both weak (Closure B); timing variation was not shown to dominate actuator-identity variation in this bounded sample (Closure C). Control opportunity in this translating-flock system continues to look predominantly stochastic/trajectory-conditioned under every intervention class and timing variant tested across the whole programme. The flock programme is closed on this basis; the next programme is morphogenesis.
why_morphogenesis_next: No further static actuator-feature search is motivated (three independent falsification passes); this closure's own Closure A/B/C results (see final_translating_flock_closure/) determine whether any structural/timing lever remains -- the program moves to morphogenesis either way, per the task's hard-stop discipline.
